checkpoints.question: A rangefinder reports distances in 1 mm increments. Does that establish that each reading is accurate to 1 mm? Explain how round-trip time relates to distance.
checkpoints.model_answer: No. Output resolution is the spacing between reported values, whereas accuracy concerns their agreement with the physical distance. In the ideal single-target geometry, light travels 2d, so d = c Delta t / 2.

checkpoints.question: A sensor uses a 200 ms timing budget. Can setting its requested publication rate to 30 Hz produce 30 new measurements per second?
checkpoints.model_answer: No. One measurement requires the allocated 200 ms, and the inter-measurement period must be at least that long. The resulting upper bound is five measurement starts per second; requesting a faster publication rate does not create additional independent measurements.

checkpoints.question: A stationary recording has a standard deviation of 2.07 mm. Does this establish that the sensor is accurate to approximately 2 mm?
checkpoints.model_answer: No. The standard deviation describes the spread of the recorded values. Accuracy requires comparison with an independently known distance. A sensor can repeatedly report similar values while retaining a systematic offset. This recording is also below the specified minimum range.

checkpoints.question: A message advertises max_range = 3.6 m. Does this guarantee that a target at 3.0 m will produce a usable reading?
checkpoints.model_answer: No. The maximum is an upper bound used by the interface and driver. Detection within that bound still depends on the target, ambient light, and measurement settings. An unavailable range may be reported even when a target is closer than 3.6 m.
